To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the emergence of OBBGs in Korea and Japan can be explained by the theories of institutionalism, market failure, transaction cost, resource based, social capital, and agency.

1) the institutional theory, transaction cost theory, resource-based theory, and social capital theory can explain the emergence and growth of business groups in developing economies; 2) the institutional theory and market failure theory can explain the formation of OBBGs in the early stage in Japan and Korea; and 3) the institutional theory can explain the evolution of OBBGs to diversified BGs in the later stage of economic development, while resource-based and social capital theories can explain the formation and growth
the institutional and resource-based theories can be applied to explain the formation of BGs in Japan and Korea, but not the market failure and transaction cost theories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical boundaries and future directions of the study of business groups (hereafter, BGs).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theories are not mutually exclusive and that they are complementary to each other.
BGs are not only a phenomenon of emerging markets but also a phenomenon of developed countries.
BG theories can explain OBBGs in the early stage, but cannot explain the evolution of BGs in the later stage of development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the business groups in Japan and Korea are not the same.
BG theories can explain OBBGs, but cannot explain the emergence of nonownership-based BGs (NOBBGs) in Japan and Korea, which emerged later than OBBGs.
the institutional environment, including the legal system and the financial system, is the most important determinant of the development of BGs in Japan and Korea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Korean business group model has not been a success.
business groups in Japan and Korea were not created by the government but by the market.
business group research should move beyond the focus on BGs as a unit of analysis and consider the role of the BG as a platform for the development of new business models.
